source: HUD FY2026 MMI Fund report via HousingWire

headline: FHA's cushion is
*5x the floor*
slides.fig_caption: FHA insurance fund capital ratio as of Sept. 30, 2026. The legal minimum is 2%.
slides.sub: A strong annual report has lenders pushing for lower mortgage insurance premiums.

slides.label: of FHA purchase loans in FY2026 went to *first-time buyers*
slides.body: That's more than 530,000 first-time buyers, out of over 935,000 total FHA borrowers.

slides.title: *Well above* the floor
slides.note: The ratio slipped 1.18 points, partly because the 2023 premium cut means newer loans bring in less revenue. It has cleared 2% for *12 straight years*.

slides.title: Will MIP *come down?*
points: The MBA wants a modest cut to annual premiums, paired with safeguards to protect the fund.
The Community Home Lenders of America wants FHA to end life-of-loan premiums, a 2013 policy.
HUD officials say they're comfortable with current capital levels, which signals no immediate premium change.

slides.title: Watch the *premium fight*
slides.body: FHA remains a key path for first-time buyers. Any cut to monthly premiums would lower payments and stretch budgets for those clients. Nothing has changed yet, so keep current MIP in your payment math for now.
